userId.description: Optional user id to send with popup events

trackingEnabled.description: Starts tracking enabled (default) or disabled (e.g. until consent is granted). Equivalent to calling `setTrackingEnabled` after init.

appVersion.description: Host app version (for analytics device info / Technology #11).

storage.description: Injectable persistent storage (RN: adapter over AsyncStorage). If missing, uses localStorage/in-memory.

platform.description: Platform used in the analytics envelope. Default is 'web'; in RN pass 'android'/'ios'.

language.description: BCP-47 language tag (e.g. 'es-ES') used for the analytics context AND for popup language segmentation (`segments.lang`). If omitted, the SDK auto-detects: `navigator.language` on web, or the `Intl` locale as a fallback (works in React Native with Hermes, where `navigator.language` is absent). If no source resolves a language, popups with `segments.lang` cannot be filtered and are shown.

device.description: Injectable device info (RN: from react-native-device-info). If missing, it is derived from the browser.

analytics.description: Analytics channel keys (`POST /sdk/feedback`). If provided, analytics is SENT to the configured integration; if missing, it stays in dry-run mode: nothing is sent, and the payload is only logged when `debug` is true.

geolocation.description: IP geolocation (country/city) added to analytics. Default `true`. The lookup calls third-party services (ipapi.co, then ipwho.is, then ipinfo.io as fallbacks, 3 s timeout each) and only runs when `analytics` is configured, tracking is enabled and the 30-day cache is missing or expired. Set `false` to never call them nor attach country/city.

contactAttributes.description: Internal user attributes known only by the host (language, age, plan, ...), sent to the backend Contact for segmentation/targeting. Requires `userId`. Equivalent to calling `setContactAttributes` after init (sends only when values changed from the last sync).

renderChrome.description: Whether the SDK renders the popup "modal" (card + backdrop + positioning) around the survey. Default `true`. Only affects React Native (the survey WebView HTML); the web DOM popup is unaffected. With `false` the survey is delivered transparent and edge-to-edge so the host mounts its own Modal/container and controls the styling — avoids the "double modal" when the host already wraps the WebView. The survey stays fully functional (bridge, form, nav buttons, close). Ver `ReactNativePopupRenderer`.

showProgressBar.description: Barra de progreso ("Question X of Y" + barra) en la cabecera del popup. Si se omite, manda el `showProgressBar` que la plataforma configura en el estilo del survey; `true` o `false` lo fuerzan desde el host. Solo se pinta con más de una página, fuera de la pantalla de inicio y antes de completar, igual que en la web de surveys.

surveyCss.description: CSS propio del host, inyectado como último bloque de estilos del popup: gana en cascada sobre el del SDK y sobre el de `@magicfeedback/native` sin tener que tocar ninguno. Es la vía para reestilar el área de preguntas (enunciados, opciones, escalas) por integración, en vez de cambiar los defaults que comparten todos los clientes.

cspNonce.description: Nonce de la Content-Security-Policy de la página, para hosts con una CSP estricta (`style-src 'nonce-…'` sin `'unsafe-inline'`). El popup lo pone en cada `<style>` que inyecta en el `<head>` (hoja del survey, spinner, responsive, `surveyCss`, `@font-face`); sin él el navegador las bloquea y el survey sale sin estilos. Debe ser el MISMO nonce de la cabecera CSP de esa respuesta (en Angular, el token `CSP_NONCE`). Solo web: en React Native el survey vive en su propio WebView y no le afecta la CSP del host.

KeyValueStorage.description: Store clave/valor mínimo (espejo conceptual del `KeyValueStorage` de KMP).

DeviceInfo.description:
Device info para el context de analytics (Technology #11–13).

En Web enviamos `device_type` + `user_agent` crudo y dejamos que el backend derive OS/navegador del UA (como hace GA). Los campos adicionales (timezone, referrer, viewport, etc.) se recogen de las APIs del navegador sin permisos. `country`/`city` se rellenan de forma asíncrona (ver geo-info.ts). En KMP las APIs nativas dan os_version/device_model reales.

PopupTrigger.description: Trigger attached to the popup definition

PopupTriggerType.description: Trigger type used by remote popup definitions

PopupTriggerCondition.description: Extra condition used to activate the popup

PopupActions.description: Set of actions available in the popup

imageUrl.deprecated: Not used by the SDK; kept only for API compatibility

font.description: Fuente personalizada. Si falta, se mantiene el comportamiento actual.

family.description: Nombre de la familia. Ej: "Inter" (nombre limpio, NO un stack).

url.description: Opcional: URL a un archivo de fuente (woff2/ttf/otf) para armar un

PopupFont.description: Fuente personalizable del popup + survey (viene de la API por popup)

excludedPaths.description: App routes where it must NOT be shown. Wins over `path`: a route listed here blocks the popup even if `path` matches it (so `path: ['/']` + `excludedPaths: ['/cart']` = everywhere but the cart). Same matching rules as `path`: an absolute URL matches the full href, an entry starting with `/` matches any href containing it (this is what covers hash routes like `/#/cart`), anything else matches the pathname exactly.

PopupSegments.description: Segments/targeting rules for showing the popup
